findings.claim: Two machine callers of `go run ./cmd/devgate build` without --out now meet the new refusal in an armed central checkout: the test run's landed re-arm rebuild (internal/testrun/rearm.go landedRearmRebuild, reached from every metasystem test run and test plan) and adoption's template build (cmd/metasystem/intent_adopt.go:178). Neither the brief nor D6c names them.
findings.evidence: cmd/metasystem/test.go:237 and :679 set LandedRearm; internal/testrun/prepare.go:319-325 calls landedRearm with no central-delivery check; rearm.go:499-506 fast-forwards, then runs DevgateBootstrapBuildArgv (no --out) in the installation. Before U2 that rebuild ran locally (forbidden by R-151-m1e); now the test run fails after the fast-forward, under a refusal that names the follow, metasystem deploy now and the escape. Not material: nothing unsafe is built and the remedy is printed. The hook rebuild (hook_entry.go:627), the steward boundary (steward_verbs.go:430), seat launch (fresh unarmed clone), the deploy and candidateengine (--out) are all safe.
findings.change: Later list: skip the test run's landed-re-arm rebuild when the installation follows the deployed engine (the follow owns that move); the steward decides adoption from an armed central template (use the deployed engine, or the escape).

findings.claim: Importing internal/steward for one path join grows devgate's compile closure from 72 to 102 internal packages (channel/slack, channel/telegram, landing/plain, supervise with a panicking init), so a compile break in any of them stops devgate itself from compiling.
findings.evidence: Measured with go list -deps ./cmd/devgate, with and without the two new imports; internal/supervise/disk.go:153-159. The brief sanctioned the import; static passes.
findings.change: Optional: join artifacts/agents/steward/identity.json inline with a comment naming steward.RepoIdentityPath.
findings.relation: new; rule: the devgate bootstrap should link only what it needs (brief item 2's inline-join alternative)

findings.claim: config.Get with no LookupEnv reads the process environment, not deps.getenv, so T11a-T11e are not hermetic against an exported engine-delivery environment variable, which in production also overrides the conf line.
findings.evidence: internal/config/resolve.go:329-332 and :365-367; the call in main.go passes no LookupEnv, exactly like followsDeployedEngine (the brief's instruction).
findings.change: Optional: make the read's environment a seam the fixture answers with unset.

findings.claim: In an armed central checkout, devgate build with an unknown argument prints the central refusal (exit 1) instead of the usage error (exit 2), because the check precedes parseBuildArgs.
findings.evidence: main.go:83-93 runs before runBuild's parseBuildArgs (build.go:23-42, :53-57). The brief places the check there.
findings.relation: new; rule: refusal precedence of usage errors
